decisions.reason: The new daily cadence and peak-hours window constrain posting time but do not change which clips may be published, their destination, or their Reel format.
Posting cadence and time do not alter the required caption, hashtags, tagged account, or tag placement.
The logging requirement remains to update the corresponding Notion card after each Reel is posted; the posting schedule does not change its trigger, destination, or fields.
The schedule change does not alter the dedicated account's creation, profile configuration, or audience-routing behavior.
Publishing one clip per day during peak hours does not change the coverage or metrics required for performance tracking.

The message confirms approval of this batch but does not change the approval authority, publication eligibility rule, correction process, or quota-counting rule; execution status must not be propagated as a MODIFY.
The publishing schedule for three approved clips does not change the completed requalification task's clip count, work, or acceptance condition.
The Instagram posting schedule does not remove or modify the existing target-channel set of Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and TikTok.
Posting cadence and peak hours do not alter the clips' completeness, educational value, or standalone-comprehension standards.
The publishing schedule does not change the permitted source material, source-video choice, exclusions, or moment-selection criteria.
The one-per-day cadence and 6 PM to 9 PM window do not alter the required 45-to-60-second clip duration.
The schedule for publishing approved clips does not change the historical initial trial's clip count, source content, or acceptance condition.
